evals.name: fod-ho-r11b
evals.prompt: 스토어 목록(필터 결과 최대 52건, 4/3/2/1열 반응형 그리드, 28/20 배치 추가 로드, filterKey 변경 시 목록 리마운트)의 렌더를 row 단위 윈도우 가상화로 교체해줘. @tanstack/react-virtual의 useWindowVirtualizer를 쓰고, 열 수의 진실 원천은 CSS 미디어쿼리로 두고 JS는 ResizeObserver로 렌더된 그리드에서 열 수를 읽기만 해. 추가 로드 트리거는 마지막 가상 row 기준으로 옮기고 IntersectionObserver sentinel은 제거. 기존 28/20 배치·filterKey 리마운트·No Result·목록 시맨틱(ul/li)·320px 리플로우는 의미 변경 없이 승계. 스크롤 컨테이너는 윈도우 그대로. Design-only로 Draft Oracle까지만.
evals.expected_output: A Draft Oracle (risk=Medium, lane=oracle) whose sweep·deviations·landmines·Open questions already carry the 4 escapes below; the run ends NEEDS_DECISION after 1 user turn.
assertions: The first line of the response is the lane header and it reports risk=Medium lane=oracle

The Draft names, in the interaction sweep, deviations, or an Open question, the StrictMode double-invoke of the effect that owns the append timer (cleanup must restore the pending state, not only clear the timer).

The Draft has a sweep cell or landmine for the inherited filterKey remount × the virtualizer's mount-time scroll reset (scrollTo / initialOffset), dispositioned as needs-decision or covered by a row that fixes the expected scroll position after remount.
The Draft names the initial default column count → first ResizeObserver measurement transition as a runtime dimension, deviation, or Open question (what is rendered before the first measurement).
The Draft raises, as an Open question or needs-decision, what the user sees during a filter switch (Suspense fallback vs the previous list kept), instead of silently inheriting the current behavior.
The Draft reaches the user after 1 turn, with every surviving question inside the Draft as an Open question

evals.name: fod-ho-vd01
evals.source: Current user proposal (2026-09-07); not a verified historical run — frontend Oracle first-Draft verification-design review
evals.prompt: Explain a type- and architecture-first plan for a server-paginated shared table library. Design only: do not implement code, add tests, install dependencies, or claim anything ran.
evals.expected_output: A Draft Oracle (risk=Medium, lane=oracle) whose sweep·deviations·landmines·Open questions already carry the 3 escapes below; the run ends NEEDS_DECISION after 1 user turn.
assertions: The first line of the response is the lane header and it reports risk=Medium lane=oracle

The first substantive Draft explicitly declares the applicable Case-space dimensions and choices (for example page mode, cache or placeholder availability, request state, and completion order), gives the constraint or applicability reason for each, and connects the risky interactions to contract rows.

For each key failure mechanism, the Draft identifies the actual hook or compound UI under test, the fetcher or deferred response boundary it controls, the observable completion barrier, the user-visible or request observation, and whether this is planned or executed evidence.

The response distinguishes protocol obligations (Draft/card/frame generation/approval and later $test handoff) from design output: it may produce a Draft and generated/dispositioned frames when the procedure calls for them, but it does not fabricate frame IDs or claim card approval, lock, or executed test evidence.
The Draft reaches the user after 1 turn, with every surviving question inside the Draft as an Open question

evals.source: Current user proposal (2026-09-07); not a verified historical run — type-only design-only boundary review
evals.prompt: Describe only the public TypeScript API and architecture for a reusable table column builder. Do not implement production code or tests. Explain how the design would verify type safety and runtime behavior.

assertions: The first line of the response is the lane header and it reports risk=Medium lane=oracle

The first Draft separates compile-time and runtime verification: it names at least one valid inference witness and one single misuse rejected by the compiler, then identifies the runtime contract, target, controllable input, and observable result without duplicating production logic.

The response preserves the design-only scope: proposed compiler witnesses and runtime harness boundaries are clearly labeled as planned examples, with no production or test-file changes, dependency installation, test execution, or fabricated PASS evidence.

The response distinguishes a legitimately produced Draft from the approval/lock protocol: it may produce the Draft and planned witnesses, but does not claim user approval, ORACLE_READY, lock, or executed test evidence, and routes unresolved policy or API decisions to Open questions.
The Draft reaches the user after 1 turn, with every surviving question inside the Draft as an Open question

The first Draft names tenant or scope, data availability (no current key, current-key cache, previous-key placeholder), request state, and completion order as applicable dimensions; it explains non-combinable or policy-unknown cells instead of treating all unions as reachable.

When Order has two or more choices, the Draft explicitly plans the existing $test sequence evidence (fast-check or justified hand-enumerated deferred orderings) and distinguishes that future execution evidence from the current first-Draft plan.

The response distinguishes protocol artifacts and gates (Draft, frame/card approval, $test handoff) from proposed verification content and reports no execution result, approval, or generated evidence that has not occurred.
